name: Launchpad Apartments (The Launchpad)
headline: Cohen-Esrey Development Group and The PLACE built The Launchpad, 50 supportive apartments for 18-to-24-year-olds leaving homelessness on North 19th Street in west Colorado Springs, all at 30% AMI with Division of Housing project-based vouchers, using $1,198,000 a year in 2022 federal 9% credits; it opened in May 2025.
why_it_matters: It is the region's first permanent supportive housing for transition-age youth and survived a neighbor appeal to City Council (denied 6-3 in August 2023) over landslide-risk and density objections, a template for defending administratively approved PSH on a sloped infill site.

status.label: Built and open (ribbon cutting 2025-05-27; move-ins June 2025)
status.detail: KRDO reported the ribbon cutting on 2025-05-27; the Pikes Peak Bulletin reported residents moving in the week of 2025-06-26; the Gazette reported in June 2026 that it had been open a year. No 8609 or placed-in-service record was found.

next_step: Confirm the 8609 year and final credit amount in CHFA or HUD placed-in-service data.

key_numbers.meaning: 47 one-bedroom and 3 two-bedroom units for young adults 18 to 24 leaving or at risk of homelessness, all with Division of Housing project-based vouchers.
About $12M over 10 years (inferred); the equity investor put in $10.9M.
Per the equity investor in early 2024: credit equity, a $2.3M CHFA permanent loan and about $5M of public soft debt.

facts.value: CHFA: 810 N. 19th Ave., Colorado Springs 80904; the narrative gives 810 N. 19th St.; just north of West Uintah and North 19th streets
N, PSH: new construction, permanent supportive housing
About 1.37 acres in Old Colorado City next to Uintah Gardens shopping center (King Soopers); hillside with a potential unstable slope on the west end; not in a 2022 QCT or DDA
Furnished units, 24-hour front desk, trauma-informed design by Shopworks; four stories and about 45 feet as presented to the Planning Commission
20-year Section 8 Housing Assistance Payment contract; tenants pay 30% of income

background.text: Development agreement: Cohen-Esrey and The PLACE agreed to share future cash flow and developer fee, and The PLACE holds a right of first offer if the owner sells.

Approvals: city staff administratively approved the development plan on 2023-05-10; neighbors appealed; the Planning Commission upheld it 6-0 in June 2023; City Council denied the further appeal 6-3 on 2023-08-08.
Appellants cited landslide risk, density and height; the developer moved the building to the northeast corner away from the slope and added a retaining wall.
Priced with Davis-Bacon wages; the narrative budgeted $100,000 for retaining walls and a $250,000 sitework reserve for the hillside.
In 2023 an El Paso County commissioner blocked a $20,750 CDBG grant for The PLACE, as reported in 2025.
Under construction in February and August 2024; the investor then expected completion in October 2024, and the building opened in May 2025.

discrepancies.text: CHFA's award and applicant reports give the address as 810 N. 19th Ave., the application narrative gives 810 N. 19th St., and a 2023 Gazette map caption places the site at 864 N. 19th St.
The 2023 Gazette reported one four-story building of about 45 feet as presented to the Planning Commission, while the 2026 Gazette describes a three-story building.
CHFA and the application describe residents aged 18 to 24, while KOAA in 2024 described the age limit as 18 to 25.
